abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pancreatic cancer is a highly lethal malignancy for which mortality remains close to incidence. We combined complementary global estimates and longitudinal cancer-registry data to characterize its current burden, recent incidence trends, and demographic implications to 2040.
METHODS: GLOBOCAN 2020 was used for cross-sectional estimates of pancreatic cancer incidence and mortality in 185 countries and territories. Continuous annual incidence trends from 2000 to 2017 were estimated from selected non-overlapping CI5plus registry populations with complete coverage over the study period. Age-standardized rates were calculated using the Segi-Doll world standard population. Log-linear models and continuous segmented regression selected by the Bayesian information criterion were used to estimate annual percentage changes (APCs). IARC Cancer Tomorrow fixed-risk demographic projections were used to estimate incident cases through 2040; annual risk-change scenarios of -0.5% and +0.5% were examined as sensitivity analyses.
RESULTS: In 2020, an estimated 495,773 pancreatic cancer cases and 466,003 deaths occurred worldwide; the ASIR and ASMR were 4.86 and 4.53 per 100,000, respectively, and the mortality-to-incidence ratio was 0.94. Northern America and Europe had the highest regional ASIRs (8.04 and 7.77), whereas Asia contributed the largest number of cases (233,701). In pooled selected CI5plus populations, incidence increased during 2000-2006 (APC 1.43%, 95% CI 1.27-1.59) and 2006-2017 (APC 1.02%, 95% CI 0.94-1.10). The relative increase was greatest among adults younger than 50 years (APC 1.61%, 95% CI 1.37-1.85), although their absolute rate remained low. Under the fixed-risk demographic scenario, global incident cases were projected to reach 843,772 in 2040, a 70.2% increase from 2020.
CONCLUSION: Pancreatic cancer imposes a substantial and geographically unequal burden, with mortality remaining close to incidence. Combining GLOBOCAN with CI5plus distinguishes contemporary global burden from observed registry-based trends and supports risk-based surveillance, registry strengthening, and health-system capacity planning.
key_points_ko: 2020년 전 세계 췌장암 신규 환자는 약 495,773명, 사망자는 약 466,003명이며 사망 대 발생 비율은 0.94였습니다.
북미와 유럽의 연령표준화 발생률(ASIR)이 가장 높았고, 아시아는 가장 많은 환자 수(233,701명)를 기록했습니다.
2000년부터 2017년까지 발병률은 2000-2006년 연간 변화율(APC) 1.43%, 2006-2017년 APC 1.02%로 꾸준히 증가했습니다.
고정 위험 시나리오 기준, 2040년 전 세계 췌장암 신규 환자는 2020년 대비 70.2% 증가한 843,772명에 달할 것으로 예측됩니다.
summary_ko: 이 연구는 GLOBOCAN 2020과 CI5plus 종단적 암 등록 데이터를 결합하여 전 세계 췌장암의 현재 부담, 최근 발병률 추세, 그리고 2040년까지의 인구통계학적 전망을 분석했습니다. 2020년 전 세계적으로 약 495,773건의 췌장암 환자가 발생하고 466,003명이 사망했으며, 사망률과 발생률의 비율은 0.94로 나타났습니다. 2000년부터 2017년까지 췌장암 발병률은 꾸준히 증가했으며, 50세 미만의 성인에서 상대적 증가 폭이 가장 컸습니다. 고정 위험 인구통계 시나리오에 따르면, 전 세계 신규 췌장암 환자는 2020년 대비 70.2% 증가한 843,772명에 이를 것으로 전망됩니다.
title: Global and registry-based patterns of pancreatic cancer: GLOBOCAN 2020, CI5plus trends (2000-2017), and demographic projections to 2040
title_ko: 전 세계 및 등록 기반 췌장암 패턴: GLOBOCAN 2020, CI5plus 추세(2000-2017), 그리고 2040년까지의 인구통계학적 전망
